## Problem

`processInMemoryWithContext` sends `Content: p.formatContent(relPath, string(content))`, and `formatContent` returns `fmt.Sprintf("\n---\n%s\n%s\n", relPath, content)`. All three writers (JSON, YAML, Markdown) then emit `req.Content` verbatim as the file's content, so the content field of every file is the real file wrapped in a leftover plain-text separator and the path a second time.

## Evidence

fileproc/processor.go:133-136: `outCh <- WriteRequest{ Path: relPath, Content: p.formatContent(relPath, string(content)), }`
fileproc/processor.go:191-192: `return fmt.Sprintf("\n---\n%s\n%s\n", relPath, content)`

Reproduced with `a.go` = `package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n`:
- JSON: `json.load(...)['files'][0]['content']` == `'\n---\na.go\npackage main\n\nfunc main() {}\n\n'`
- YAML: parsed content == `'\n---\na.go\npackage main\n\nfunc main() {}\n'`
- Markdown: the fenced block contains a blank line, `---`, `a.go`, then the code.

fileproc/processor_test.go:70 asserts `strings.Contains(result, tmpFile.Name())` — the test requires the path to be inside Content, encoding the defect.

## Impact

The tool's sole output is wrong for every file: consumers parsing `content` get bytes that are not the file, Markdown code blocks start with a stray `---` line (renders as a horizontal rule inside the code), and every file pays extra tokens for a duplicated path. Any downstream that diffs or hashes content sees a mismatch.

## Fix

Delete `formatContent` and send `Content: string(content)`. Update `TestProcessFile` to assert `result == content` and `req.Path == relPath` instead of `Contains(result, path)`. When the header is gone the YAML writer becomes the first place a leading-whitespace line can start the block scalar: change `shared.YAMLFmtFileEntry` to `"    content: |2\n"` (explicit indentation indicator) and use a keep/strip chomping indicator that round-trips the file's trailing newline; add a writer test that parses YAML output for content starting with spaces and for content with no trailing newline and asserts exact equality.

## Resolution
formatContent removed; WriteRequest.Content is the file's bytes. YAML block scalar now uses an explicit indentation indicator (|2) and per-file chomping (+/-) so content round-trips exactly. TestProcessFileContentIsExact and TestStructuredOutputRoundTrips (JSON+YAML: leading spaces, no/extra trailing newlines, empty) assert exact equality; the old Contains(path) assertion was removed.

## Problem

`startFormatWriter` returns (closing `done`) as soon as `writer.Start` fails, without consuming `writeCh`. Workers block forever on `outCh <- WriteRequest{...}` (fileproc/processor.go:130-137) because the CLI context is `context.Background()` and never cancels; `waitForCompletion` blocks on `wg.Wait()` forever.

## Evidence

fileproc/writer.go:25-29:
```go
if err := writer.Start(prefix, suffix); err != nil {
	shared.LogError("Failed to start writer", err)
	return
}
```
Reproduced: 300 files, `-destination /dev/full -format json -concurrency 2` → `timeout 15` kills it (exit 124). With 1 file the 64-slot buffer absorbs the send and it exits 0 instead (see the swallowed-errors finding). The `default:` branch of `StartWriter` (writer.go:53-65) has the same shape.

## Impact

Disk full, quota exceeded, or any write error on the prefix makes the CLI hang indefinitely on any repository with more files than channel buffer + workers — in CI that is a stuck job until the runner timeout.

## Fix

On Start failure, keep draining: `for range writeCh {}` before returning, and report the error (see the swallowed-errors finding for propagating it). Same for the unsupported-format branch. Add a test that runs `StartWriter` with an `*os.File` opened read-only (Start's write fails) while a producer sends > channelBuffer requests, asserting the producer finishes and `done` closes within a timeout.

## Resolution
StartWriter now returns its error and runFormatWriter keeps draining writeCh after a Start/WriteFile failure (unsupported formats go through the same path). TestStartWriterDrainsAfterStartFailure (200 sends on an unbuffered channel) and TestProcessWriteFailureReturnsErrorWithoutHanging (/dev/full, 3x buffer files) guard it; the 300-file /dev/full repro now exits 1 instead of hanging.
title: Writer Start failure returns without draining writeCh, deadlocking all workers and hanging the process

Every failure after flag validation is logged and dropped: `writer.WriteFile`/`writer.Close` errors (writer.go:32-41), the output file's `Close` error (cli/processor_processing.go:64-66), and per-file processing errors (cli/processor_workers.go:52-54). `processFiles` returns nil and prints "Processing completed. Output saved to …". There is no error channel from the writer and no failure counter.

## Evidence

fileproc/writer.go:33-35: `if err := writer.WriteFile(req); err != nil { shared.LogError("Failed to write file", err) }`
cli/processor_workers.go:52-53: `} else if err := fileproc.ProcessFileContext(...); err != nil { shared.LogErrorf(err, "processing file %s", filePath) }`

Reproduced:
- `-destination /dev/full` (1 file): exit 0, nothing written.
- Source with an unreadable `b.go` (chmod 000): exit 0, `✓ Processing completed. Output saved to o3.json`, output contains only `a.go`; with `-no-ui` the only signal is two `level=error` lines.

## Impact

Scripts, CI and git hooks (examples/basic-usage.md:158-179) cannot detect truncated or incomplete output. A disk-full run leaves a syntactically broken JSON file and a zero exit status; a permission problem silently drops files from the LLM context.

## Fix

Make the writer report its first error: change `done chan<- struct{}` to `done chan<- error` (or add an `errCh`), send the first Start/WriteFile/Close error, and return it from `waitForCompletion`/`processFiles`. Count per-file failures in `processFile` (atomic counter) and return a structured error (`ErrorTypeProcessing`) from `Process` when the count is > 0, after the output is written, so the exit status is non-zero. Return `outFile.Close()`'s error instead of logging it. Add CLI tests asserting non-zero exit for the /dev/full and unreadable-file cases.

## Resolution
Writer, output Close and per-file failures now reach processFiles: write/close errors return an IO error (output removed), per-file failures are counted (runStats) and return a Processing error after the output is written. Verified: /dev/full exits 1 "failed to write output"; unreadable file exits 1 "1 of 2 files could not be processed". Tests: TestProcessFailsWhenAFileCannotBeRead, TestStartWriterReadOnlyFileReturnsError.
title: Write, close and per-file read failures are only logged; the run reports success and exits 0

body:
## Problem

Nothing excludes the destination path from collection. The default destination is `<basename>.<format>` in the current directory (cli/flags.go:125-131), so running from inside the source directory — or using a destination under the source as the docs recommend (`-source . -destination docs/codebase.md`, examples/basic-usage.md:114-116, 164, 178) — puts the previous output into the next run's input. `createOutputFile` truncates the destination after collection, so the worker then reads a file that the writer is concurrently writing.

## Evidence

Reproduced in a temp dir with `cd src2 && gibidify -source . -format json` twice:
- run 1 paths: `['.gitignore', 'sub/keep.go', 'sub/drop.log', 'a.go']`
- run 2 paths: `['a.go', 'sub/drop.log', 'sub/keep.go', '.gitignore', 'src2.json']`
fileproc/walker.go:66-87 appends every non-skipped entry; no comparison against the destination exists anywhere (`rg Destination fileproc/` has no hits).

## Impact

Each re-run embeds a partial copy of the tool's own output into the LLM context (growing, self-referential, and racy content), wasting tokens and producing nondeterministic garbage — on exactly the workflows the examples document (git pre-commit hook, Makefile target, CI).

## Fix

Resolve the destination to an absolute path in `setDefaultDestination` and pass it to the walker (e.g. `NewProdWalker(excludePaths ...string)` / a `FileFilter.excluded` set); skip an entry whose absolute path equals it (compare after `filepath.Clean`; on case-insensitive filesystems also `os.SameFile` against a stat taken before truncation). Add a test that runs `Process` twice with destination inside source and asserts the second output lists the same paths as the first.

## Resolution
collectFiles passes the absolute destination to CollectFiles/NewProdWalker(excludePaths...), and FileFilter skips it. Repro (two runs in the source dir) now lists the same paths both times. Tests: TestProdWalkerExcludesPaths, TestProcessDoesNotIngestOwnOutput.
title: The output file is re-ingested as input on every subsequent run when the destination is inside the source tree

body:
## Problem

The walker treats every non-directory `DirEntry` as a file — a symlink's `entry.IsDir()` is false — and `readCapped` opens it with `os.Open`, which follows the link. A symlink in the scanned tree to any file the user can read (`~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `/etc/…`) is emitted into the output under the link's in-tree name. The source-path "traversal" validation (shared/paths.go) gives no protection because the link target is never checked.

## Evidence

fileproc/walker.go:74-87: `if entry.IsDir() { … walkDir … } else { results = append(results, fullPath) }`
fileproc/processor.go:146: `f, err := os.Open(filePath) // #nosec G304 - filePath is validated by walker`

Reproduced: `src5/link.txt -> ../outside/secret.txt` containing `TOP-SECRET-OUTSIDE-TREE`. Output (exit 0) contains `link.txt` with content `…TOP-SECRET-OUTSIDE-TREE…`. A symlinked directory (`linkdir`) is instead opened as a file, fails with a read error, is logged twice and dropped.

## Impact

The documented use is pasting a repository into an LLM (examples/basic-usage.md:197-200, "AI Code Analysis"), including third-party repos. A malicious repository can plant `README.txt -> ../../.aws/credentials`; the user's secrets then go to the model provider, with no warning. The `#nosec G304` comment asserts a validation that does not exist.

## Fix

In `walkDir`, check `entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0` and skip symlinks by default (log at Info). If following links is wanted, gate it behind an explicit flag and require `filepath.EvalSymlinks(target)` to stay under the absolute source root (`strings.HasPrefix(resolved, root+string(os.PathSeparator))`). In `readCapped`, open with `os.Lstat` check first so a file swapped for a symlink after collection is refused. Correct the `#nosec G304` justification. Add walker tests for an in-tree symlink, an out-of-tree file symlink, and a directory symlink.

## Resolution
FileFilter skips every symlink and non-regular file (FIFOs, sockets, devices); validateFile uses Lstat and refuses non-regular files at read time, returning ErrSkipped. The #nosec G304 justification was corrected. Repro now emits only a.go. Tests: TestProdWalkerSkipsSymlinks, TestProdWalkerSkipsFIFO, TestProcessorRefusesSymlink.
title: Symlinks inside the source tree are followed, pulling files from outside the tree into the LLM-bound output

body:
## Problem

`Dockerfile:8` is `COPY --chmod=0755 gibidify /usr/local/bin/gibidify`, but `.dockerignore:7` lists `gibidify`, so the file is never in the build context. Separately, the `docker` job in build-test-publish.yml (lines 143-185) checks out source and runs `docker buildx build … .` with no `go build` step and no artifact download, so there is no binary even without the ignore rule. That job also pushes to `ghcr.io/${repo}/gibidify` = `ghcr.io/ivuorinen/gibidify/gibidify`, a different image than the `ghcr.io/ivuorinen/gibidify` that goreleaser (release.yml) publishes and README documents.

## Evidence

Reproduced: context containing `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, and a freshly built `gibidify` binary → `docker build` fails: `failed to compute cache key: … "/gibidify": not found` (exit 1).
.dockerignore:6-7: `# Build artifacts` / `gibidify`
build-test-publish.yml:181-185: `repo="$(echo "$GH_REPOSITORY" | tr …)"; docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --tag "ghcr.io/${repo}/gibidify:${REF_NAME}" …`

## Impact

README's `docker build -t ghcr.io/ivuorinen/gibidify:<tag> .` fails for every user, and the `docker` job fails on every GitHub release event. Two release pipelines (goreleaser on tag push, build-test-publish on release) disagree on the image name, so a fixed job would publish a second, undocumented image.

## Fix

Delete the `docker` job from build-test-publish.yml; goreleaser's `dockers`/`docker_manifests` already publish multi-arch images on tag push. Make the root Dockerfile build from source so `docker build .` works: a `golang:<pinned>` builder stage running `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /out/gibidify .`, then `COPY --from=builder /out/gibidify /usr/local/bin/gibidify`; keep `gibidify` in .dockerignore (the stage builds it). Keep goreleaser's inline Dockerfile for release images.

## Resolution
Dockerfile is now multi-stage (golang:1.27.2-alpine3.24 builder, digest-pinned) so `docker build .` works; verified build + run (-version) and uid 10001. The broken release-triggered docker job and the release trigger were removed from build-test-publish.yml; goreleaser (release.yml) remains the only image publisher. hadolint clean.
title: Dockerfile cannot build: it COPYs the gibidify binary that .dockerignore excludes, and the release docker job never builds one

body:
## Problem

`make lint` runs `pre-commit run --all-files`. The pre-commit hooks `go run` their own pinned versions — staticcheck v0.7.0, gosec v2.24.0, golangci-lint v2.10.1 — while the Makefile pins v0.8.1, v2.29.0, v2.14.0 and security.yml pins gosec v2.26.1 / golangci-lint v2.14.0. The pre-commit versions cannot read go1.27 export data, so three hooks fail on internal errors before analysing anything. Renovate updates the Makefile and workflow pins but not the `entry:` lines, despite the `# renovate:` comments.

## Evidence

.pre-commit-config.yaml:58 `staticcheck@v0.7.0`, :67 `gosec@v2.24.0`, :88 `golangci-lint@v2.10.1`; Makefile:13 `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION := v2.14.0`, :21 `GOSEC_VERSION := v2.29.0`, :23 `STATICCHECK_VERSION := v0.8.1`; security.yml:51 `gosec@v2.26.1`.
`pre-commit run --all-files`: staticcheck Failed (`export data version 4 is greater than maximum supported version 2`), gosec Failed (`package "errors" without types was imported`), golangci-lint Failed (4 typecheck issues), govulncheck Failed (separate finding).
Same code with the Makefile pins: `make lint-static` exit 0, `make lint-sec` exit 0, `make lint-golangci` `0 issues.` (each control-checked against a planted U1000/G204/errcheck case).

## Impact

CLAUDE.md declares `make lint-fix && make lint` must show 0 issues; it cannot pass for anyone on the repo's own toolchain, so contributors either skip the gate or chase phantom failures, and real lint regressions are hidden behind tool crashes.

## Fix

Remove the duplication instead of re-syncing it: change the staticcheck, gosec, golangci-lint (and revive) pre-commit hooks to `entry: make lint-static` / `make lint-sec` / `make lint-golangci` / `make lint-go`, so the Makefile is the single pin source Renovate already maintains. Have security.yml call the same make targets (or read the version from the Makefile) instead of its own pins.

## Resolution
Pre-commit tool hooks now call make lint-go/lint-static/lint-sec/lint-golangci/vuln-check, and security.yml calls make gosec-sarif/vuln-sarif/lint-golangci/lint-shell, so the Makefile is the single pin source. `make lint` now passes all 10 hooks. staticcheck had to move to v0.8.2 (released 2026-10-12) because v0.8.1 cannot read go1.27.2 export data.
title: `make lint` (the mandatory gate) fails on clean code because pre-commit pins tools too old for the go1.27 toolchain; versions are duplicated in three places and have drifted

body:
## Problem

N workers send `WriteRequest`s to one channel in completion order and the writer emits them in arrival order. The walker's sorted `os.ReadDir` order is discarded, so identical input produces differently ordered output on every run.

## Evidence

cli/processor_workers.go:20-23 starts `p.flags.Concurrency` workers on a shared `fileCh`; fileproc/writer.go:32 `for req := range writeCh` writes in receive order.
Reproduced: 300-file source, three consecutive runs, md5 of the concatenated path list: `5a78bc99…`, `3ac5d03c…`, `3af736a1…` (all different).

## Impact

Outputs cannot be diffed, cached, or committed (e.g. the documented `docs/codebase.md` pre-commit hook rewrites the whole file on every commit); LLM prompt caching keyed on prefix misses every time; related files are scattered instead of grouped by directory.

## Fix

Carry the collection index in `WriteRequest` (`Index int`) and have the writer emit in index order using a small reorder buffer (`map[int]WriteRequest` plus `next int`), or collect results into a slice indexed by position and write after `wg.Wait()` (memory is already bounded by fileSizeLimit × in-flight). Add a test that runs `Process` with concurrency 8 over 200 files and asserts output paths equal the sorted collection order.

## Resolution
Ordered fan-out: sendFiles queues each job's result channel in collection order and a sequence goroutine forwards results to the writer in that order (bounded by the channel buffer). Three runs over 300 files now hash identically. Test: TestProcessOutputOrderIsDeterministic (200 files, concurrency 8).
title: Output file order is nondeterministic across runs on the same input

body:
## Problem

`run` calls `cli.ParseFlags()` (which calls `ValidateConcurrency`) and only afterwards `config.LoadConfig()`. `ValidateConcurrency` checks the ceiling only `if IsSet(shared.ConfigKeyMaxConcurrency)`, which is always false at that point. The registered default `ConfigMaxConcurrencyDefault = 32` is also dead, since `IsSet` ignores defaults, and `MaxConcurrency()`'s comment ("Returns 0 if not set") contradicts that default.

## Evidence

main.go:52 `flags, err := cli.ParseFlags()` … main.go:68 `config.LoadConfig()`.
config/validation.go:276-286: `if IsSet(shared.ConfigKeyMaxConcurrency) { … concurrency > maxConcurrency … }`.
Reproduced: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` config with `maxConcurrency: 2`, `-concurrency 50` → `ℹ Workers: 50`, exit 0; debug log confirms the config file was loaded.
Commit 658eec6's message claims the opposite: "Keeps maxConcurrency, which ValidateConcurrency still uses as a ceiling on the -concurrency flag."

## Impact

A documented setting (config.example.yaml:38-40, configuration-examples.md) is a no-op; users who cap workers for shared CI runners get uncapped concurrency.

## Fix

Call `config.LoadConfig()` before `cli.ParseFlags()` in `run` (LoadConfig does not depend on flags; set the log level after parsing or re-log). Alternatively drop the `maxConcurrency` setting and its docs entirely if no ceiling is wanted. Either way delete the dead default or make `MaxConcurrency()`'s comment true. Add a `run` test with a temp config containing `maxConcurrency: 2` and `-concurrency 3` that expects a validation error.

## Resolution
run() re-validates -concurrency with config.ValidateConcurrency after config.LoadConfig(). The dead maxConcurrency default (32) and its constant were removed so MaxConcurrency() returns 0 when unset, matching its doc. Repro (maxConcurrency: 2, -concurrency 50) now exits 1. Test: TestRunEnforcesConfiguredMaxConcurrency.
title: maxConcurrency from config is never enforced: flags are validated before the config file is loaded

body:
## Problem

`ReadInConfig` returns distinct errors for "no file found", "reading config file" and "parsing config file", but `LoadConfig` logs all three at Info and continues with defaults. Default level is WARN, so a YAML syntax error or permission error in the user's config produces no output at all.

## Evidence

config/loader.go:39-41: `if err := ReadInConfig(); err != nil { logger.Infof("No usable config file, using default values: %v", err); return }`
config/store.go:119-124 returns `reading config file %s` / `parsing config file %s` errors.
Reproduced: config containing `fileSizeLimit: [oops` → no stderr output, exit 0, defaults used. By contrast a well-formed but invalid value (`fileSizeLimit: 10`) does print a `level=warn` line.

## Impact

A typo in `~/.config/gibidify/config.yaml` silently discards every setting (ignore dirs, size caps, custom languages), and the user has no way to learn why their config has no effect.

## Fix

Distinguish not-found from the rest: have `ReadInConfig` return a sentinel (`errNoConfigFile`) for the not-found case; in `LoadConfig` log that at Info and log read/parse errors at Warn (matching the existing validation-failure path), or return the error so the CLI exits non-zero. Add a loader test asserting a Warn-level message for malformed YAML.

## Resolution
ReadInConfig returns errNoConfigFile for the not-found case; LoadConfig logs that at Info and read/parse failures at Warn (fallback message also Warn). Tests: TestLoadConfigMalformedFileWarns, TestLoadConfigMissingFileIsQuiet.
title: A malformed or unreadable config file is ignored silently at the default log level

body:
## Problem

`shouldSkipFile` skips a file only if `IsBinary(fullPath) || IsImage(fullPath)`, which consult extension maps. Executables without an extension, data blobs, and any binary format not in the list are read and written as text; `json.Marshal` replaces invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD.

## Evidence

fileproc/file_filters.go:55-56: `return IsBinary(fullPath) || IsImage(fullPath)`.
Reproduced: `blob` (4096 random bytes) → emitted, 3937 chars, 1792 U+FFFD; `runme` (copy of /usr/bin/true) → emitted, 26876 chars, 6785 U+FFFD. `x.db` (same bytes, listed extension) is skipped.

## Impact

Compiled tools, test fixtures and data files committed without extensions fill the LLM context with up to fileSizeLimit (5MB) of replacement characters per file, wasting tokens and degrading the output the tool exists to produce.

## Fix

After the extension check, sniff content: in `readCapped` (or the walker) inspect the first 8000 bytes and treat the file as binary if it contains a NUL byte or `!utf8.Valid(head)` (git's heuristic); skip it with an Info log. Add a processor test with an extensionless file containing `\x00` that must not appear in output.

## Resolution
processInMemoryWithContext skips (ErrSkipped) any file with a NUL byte in its first 8000 bytes (git's heuristic); skips are counted, not failed. Repro: blob and runme no longer appear in output. Test: TestProcessorSkipsBinaryContent.
title: Binary detection is extension-only: extensionless or unlisted binaries are emitted as mangled text

body:
## Problem

`shouldSkipEntry` applies `.gitignore`/`.ignore` rules only to files; directories are skipped only by the `ignoreDirectories` name list. The walker therefore descends into every gitignored directory (`venv/`, `.venv/`, `coverage/`, `.next/`, …) and evaluates every file inside against all accumulated rules. `walkDir` turns any `os.ReadDir` failure into a hard error that unwinds the entire collection.

## Evidence

fileproc/file_filters.go:26-28: `if entry.IsDir() { return f.shouldSkipDirectory(entry) }` (name list only).
fileproc/walker.go:54-62 and 75-83 return the ReadDir/subdirectory error upward.
Reproduced: `.gitignore` = `venv/`, `venv/locked` chmod 000 → `level=error msg="System error: … failed to read directory: …/venv/locked: permission denied"`, `✗ An unexpected error occurred`, exit 2, no output — for a directory the user explicitly ignored.

## Impact

Runs on Python/Node projects walk hundreds of thousands of ignored files (time is O(files × rules)); a single root-owned or permission-restricted cache directory (common for Docker volume mounts) makes the tool unusable on that repository.

## Fix

In `shouldSkipEntry`, also check `matchesIgnoreRules(fullPath+"/", rules)` (or the dir form go-gitignore expects) for directories, so ignored directories are pruned before `walkDir` recurses. In `walkDir`, log and skip an unreadable subdirectory instead of returning the error (keep failing only for the root). Add walker tests: gitignored directory with an unreadable child succeeds; gitignored directory's files are absent.

## Resolution
Directories are now matched against .gitignore/.ignore rules with a trailing slash (go-gitignore's directory form) and pruned before descent; an unreadable subdirectory is logged at Warn and skipped (only the root still fails). Repro (gitignored venv/ with a mode-000 child) exits 0. Tests: TestProdWalkerPrunesGitignoredDirectories, TestProdWalkerSkipsUnreadableSubdirectory.
title: Gitignored directories are fully traversed, and any unreadable directory anywhere aborts the whole run

body:
## Problem

`ValidateSourcePath` and `ValidateDestinationPath` reject any path whose string contains `..` (substring, not path element), and `ValidateSourcePath` rejects relative paths that resolve outside the CWD — but absolute paths skip the CWD check entirely. For a local CLI run by the user on their own files there is no trust boundary to defend; the checks only block valid input.

## Evidence

shared/paths.go:46: `if strings.Contains(path, "..") {` ; shared/paths.go:67: `if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {` (CWD boundary check only for relative paths); same substring check at :143.
Reproduced: `cd d1 && gibidify -source ../src1` → `✗ Error: path traversal attempt detected in source path`, exit 1; directory `a..b` → same error, exit 1; `-destination ../out.json` is likewise rejected; `-source /etc` passes the check.

## Impact

Users cannot point the tool at a sibling directory or write output next to the project without converting to absolute paths, and directories with `..` in their name are unusable; the error message misdescribes normal input as an attack.

## Fix

Delete the `..` substring checks and the CWD-boundary block from `ValidateSourcePath`/`ValidateDestinationPath`; keep the existence/is-directory/parent-exists checks, which are the real validation. (Containment of what is *read* belongs in the walker — see the symlink finding.) Update the `shared/paths_test.go` cases that assert traversal rejection, and `ValidateConfigPath` the same way.

## Resolution
Removed the ".." substring and CWD-boundary checks from ValidateSourcePath/ValidateDestinationPath and deleted ValidateConfigPath (LoadConfig now ignores a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME per the XDG spec). CodeValidationPath value renamed PATH_TRAVERSAL -> INVALID_PATH. `-source ../src1` and `-source a..b` now succeed. paths_test cases updated to assert acceptance.
title: Path "traversal" checks reject legitimate paths (`../proj`, names containing "..") while allowing any absolute path

body:
## Problem

`IsUserError` accepts a `StructuredError` only when `Type == ErrorTypeValidation` (the two `Code` checks are subsets of that). User mistakes that `ValidateSourcePath`/`ValidateDestinationPath` classify as `ErrorTypeFileSystem` — source does not exist, destination parent missing — fall through to main's system-error path. Consequently `provideFileSystemSuggestions`, `provideProcessingSuggestions` and `provideIOSuggestions` (cli/errors.go:91-159) are never reached from `main`.

## Evidence

cli/errors.go:271-276: `if errors.As(err, &structErr) { return structErr.Type == shared.ErrorTypeValidation || … }`
main.go:36-40: system errors log `System error: %v` and print `An unexpected error occurred. Please check the logs.`, exit 2.
Reproduced: `-source nope` → `level=error msg="System error: … source directory does not exist"` + `✗ An unexpected error occurred. Please check the logs.`, exit 2. `-destination /nonexistent/x.json` → exit 2.

## Impact

The most common user mistake (mistyped path) is presented as an internal failure, and ~70 lines of suggestion code exist only for tests.

## Fix

Treat every `*StructuredError` returned from `ParseFlags` as a user error (wrap flag-validation failures in a dedicated type, or have `run` call `errorFormatter.FormatError` for any error from `cli.ParseFlags`), and route processing-time IO errors through `FormatError` as well. If the FS/IO/Processing suggestion branches are still unreachable after that, delete them.

## Resolution
IsUserError treats every StructuredError as user-facing, so FileSystem/IO/Processing errors go through ErrorFormatter with their suggestions (now reachable). Missing source prints "source directory does not exist" + FileSystem suggestions and exits 1. errors_test case updated.
title: FileSystem/IO-typed user errors are reported as "An unexpected error occurred" (exit 2); their suggestion branches are unreachable

body:
## Problem

When `sendFiles` returns an error, `processFiles` returns immediately: it never closes `writeCh` or waits for workers/writer, so the writer goroutine blocks forever on `range writeCh` while the deferred `outFile.Close()` runs concurrently with any write it is performing. Meanwhile `main` passes `context.Background()` and installs no signal handling, so all of the context plumbing (`CheckContextCancellation`, `select ctx.Done()`) is unreachable in production and Ctrl-C kills the process mid-write, leaving a truncated output file with no message.

## Evidence

cli/processor_processing.go:85-89: `if err := p.sendFiles(ctx, files, fileCh); err != nil { p.ui.FinishProgress(); return err }` — no `close(writeCh)`, no `wg.Wait()`, no `<-writerDone`.
cli/processor_processing.go:64-66: deferred `outFile.Close()`.
main.go:30: `run(context.Background())`.
cli/processor_test.go:629-630 exercises the cancelled path (`cancel() // Cancel immediately`) and passes, leaking the goroutine.

## Impact

Any embedding or future signal handling hits a goroutine leak and a write-after-close race on the output; today an interrupted run leaves a half-written JSON/YAML file that looks like a valid output path.

## Fix

Use `ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` in `main`. In `processFiles`, always run the shutdown sequence on every return path: `defer func() { wg.Wait(); close(writeCh); <-writerDone; outFile.Close() }()` ordered so the file closes last, and on cancellation remove the partial destination (or write to a temp file in the same directory and `os.Rename` on success). Add a test under `-race` that cancels mid-run and asserts no goroutine remains (`goleak` or a `runtime.NumGoroutine` check).

## Resolution
main uses signal.NotifyContext (SIGINT/SIGTERM). processFiles runs the full shutdown on every path (send loop, wg.Wait, writer result) before closing the file; workers drain all jobs and close every job's result channel, so nothing leaks. Canceled or failed-write runs remove the partial output (regular files only). sendFiles checks ctx.Err() each iteration. Tests: TestProcessCanceledRemovesPartialOutput, TestIntegrationCancellation (asserts removal); suite passes -race -count=2 -shuffle=on.
title: Cancellation path leaks the writer goroutine and closes the output file under it; nothing in main ever cancels

body:
## Problem

go.mod pins `toolchain go1.27.1`. govulncheck reports GO-2026-6617, GO-2026-6613, GO-2026-6611 and GO-2026-6603 (net/http, net/http/internal/http2) as called, all fixed in go1.27.2. The traces go through interface dispatch (`fmt.Fprintf` → `io.Writer`), so actual exploitability in this CLI, which runs no HTTP server, is nil; but govulncheck exits 3 and both the pre-commit hook and security.yml's "Parse govulncheck results" step fail on `level == "error"` results.

## Evidence

go.mod:5 `toolchain go1.27.1`.
`govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 4 vulnerabilities from the Go standard library." Each: `Found in: net/http…@go1.27.1  Fixed in: …@go1.27.2`; example trace `fileproc/markdown_writer.go:45:27: fileproc.MarkdownWriter.Close calls fmt.Fprintf, which eventually calls http2.bufferedWriterTimeoutWriter.Write`. Exit 3.

## Impact

Security CI and `make lint` stay red until the toolchain moves; released binaries are built with a stdlib that has known advisories, which downstream scanners (grype/trivy on the binary) will flag.

## Fix

Set `toolchain go1.27.2` in go.mod (Renovate's toolchain manager already tracks this directive, cf. #273) and re-run `govulncheck ./...` to confirm 0 called vulnerabilities.

## Resolution
go.mod toolchain go1.27.1 -> go1.27.2; govulncheck now reports "No vulnerabilities found."
title: Toolchain go1.27.1 carries 4 govulncheck-reachable stdlib vulnerabilities; the govulncheck gate fails

body:
## Problem

`Flags.Verbose` is set by `fs.BoolVar(&flags.Verbose, "verbose", …)` and referenced nowhere else in production code. The documented behavior does not exist.

## Evidence

`rg 'Verbose' --type go -g '!*_test.go'` → only cli/flags.go:25 (field) and :63 (registration).
README.md:57: "`--verbose`: enable verbose output and detailed logging."
examples/basic-usage.md:132 "This will warn about permission issues but continue … --verbose"; :153 "Use `--verbose` to see memory usage during processing".
CLAUDE.md:22-23 shows `--verbose` in the canonical commands.

## Impact

security.yml:125-126: `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace \ aquasec/trivy:latest fs --security-checks vuln,config /workspace/Dockerfile || true`; :70 `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest`; :112 `go install mvdan.cc/sh/v3/cmd/shfmt@latest`. A broken or compromised trivy/govulncheck/shfmt release runs in a job with `security-events: write`; the Docker scan reports green even when it errors or finds issues.

## Problem

`EscapeForYAML` wraps in double quotes and escapes only `\` and `"`. A raw newline inside a YAML double-quoted scalar is folded to a space, and other control characters are invalid there. It is used for prefix, suffix and file paths.

## Evidence

shared/writers.go:59-62: `escaped := strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\\", "\\\\"); escaped = strings.ReplaceAll(escaped, "\"", "\\\"")`.
Reproduced: `-format yaml -prefix $'line1\nline2'` → `yaml.safe_load(...)['prefix'] == 'line1 line2'`.

## Impact

YAML output does not round-trip the user's prefix/suffix (often a multi-line instruction block for the LLM); a filename containing a control character produces unparsable YAML.

## Fix

Use the JSON encoding for the quoted form — a JSON string literal is a valid YAML double-quoted scalar: `b, _ := json.Marshal(content); return string(b)` when quoting is needed (or always). Add a test that parses YAML output with a multi-line prefix and asserts equality.

## Resolution
EscapeForYAML always emits a JSON-encoded string (valid YAML double-quoted syntax, HTML escaping off), escaping newlines and control characters; language values are escaped too. Multi-line prefix now round-trips ('line1\nline2'). writers_test expectations updated; TestStructuredOutputRoundTrips covers prefix/suffix.
title: EscapeForYAML does not escape newlines or control characters: multi-line prefix/suffix and paths are altered

## Problem

Any validation error makes `LoadConfig` replace the entire configuration with defaults and continue the run. `validateIgnoreDirectories` treats every dot-prefixed name except `.git`, `.vscode` and `.idea` as an error ("starts with dot - this may cause unexpected behavior"), so common entries such as `.venv`, `.next`, `.terraform`, `.cache` or `.idea-local` reject the file. Every other setting in it goes with it, including the user's other `ignoreDirectories` entries.

## Evidence

config/loader.go:60-66:
```go
if err := ValidateConfig(); err != nil {
	logger.Warnf("Configuration validation failed: %v", err)
	logger.Warnf("Falling back to default configuration")
	Reset()
	SetDefaultConfig()
}
```
config/validation.go:168: `if strings.HasPrefix(dir, ".") && dir != ".git" && dir != ".vscode" && dir != ".idea" {`

Reproduced with the built binary: config `ignoreDirectories: [secrets, .venv]`, tree `secrets/creds.txt`, `.venv/lib.py`, `main.py`. `gibidify -source src -destination o.json -no-ui` exits 0 and the output's files are `['.venv/lib.py', 'main.py', 'secrets/creds.txt']`. Both directories the user excluded are included.

A config file that exists but cannot be read or parsed takes the same path. config/loader.go:44-51 logs `Ignoring config file, using default values` at Warn and returns. Reproduced: config `ignoreDirectories: [secrets` (missing `]`) → exit 0, output `['secrets/k.txt']`.

## Impact

A directory the user excluded to keep credentials or private data out of an LLM prompt is included, and the run reports success. The only signal is two Warn lines on stderr. The trigger is an ordinary entry (`.venv`), not a malformed file.

## Fix

Make a config validation error fatal, and likewise a read or parse error of a config file that exists. Only `errNoConfigFile` may continue on defaults. Have `LoadConfig` return the error, and have `run` in main.go return it as a configuration user error (exit 1) instead of continuing on defaults. Delete the dot-prefix rule at config/validation.go:168-173: a dot directory is a valid directory name, and `shouldSkipDirectory` compares names exactly. Add a loader test asserting that an invalid config fails the run, plus a test that `.venv` is accepted.

## Resolution
LoadConfig returns an error for an unreadable, unparseable or invalid config file (only a missing file continues on defaults); run() returns it as a Configuration user error (exit 1) with config suggestions. Dot-prefix rule deleted. Tests: TestLoadConfigInvalidValueFails, TestLoadConfigMalformedFileFails, TestLoadConfigAcceptsDotDirectories, TestRunFailsOnInvalidConfig. Repro (secrets/.venv config) now exits 1 with no output. Docs updated (README, config.example.yaml, configuration-examples.md).
title: One rejected ignoreDirectories entry discards the whole config, so the user's exclusions are dropped and excluded files reach the output

## Problem

`writeInline` copies raw file bytes into a `|2` literal block scalar line by line. YAML allows only printable characters in a block scalar: no C0 controls other than TAB/LF, no DEL or C1 controls, and the stream must be valid UTF-8. CR is a line break in YAML. So one file with an ANSI escape (ESC), a form feed, a bare CR or a Latin-1 byte makes the whole document fail to parse. CRLF files parse but lose every `\r`, which contradicts the code comment that the parsed value equals the file "byte-for-byte". `shared.EscapeForYAML`, used for path/prefix/suffix, has the same gap: JSON encoding leaves DEL and C1 controls unescaped.

## Evidence

Built binary, `-format yaml`, one file per run, then parsed with PyYAML `safe_load` and the project's own `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`:
- `printf 'x\033[31mred\n'`: PyYAML "unacceptable character #x001b"; yaml.v3 "yaml: control characters are not allowed"
- `printf 'a\rb\n'`: PyYAML ScannerError
- `printf 'caf\xe9\n'`: PyYAML "invalid continuation byte"
- `printf 'a\r\nb\r\n'`: parses, content `'a\nb\n'` (want `'a\r\nb\r\n'`)

Every run exited 0.

## Impact

The documented YAML format produces a file no YAML consumer can load whenever the tree holds one such file: ANSI fixtures, C sources with `^L`, Windows text, legacy-encoded sources. The tool reports success. CRLF content is altered without notice.

## Fix

Emit each entry with the YAML encoder already in go.mod instead of hand-formatting: `yaml.NewEncoder(w)` on a one-element `[]FileData` per `WriteFile` (indent 2). It picks literal style for printable multi-line text and double-quoted escapes otherwise, so every string round-trips. Do the same for the prefix/suffix header and drop `EscapeForYAML`. For invalid UTF-8, decide explicitly (skip with a logged reason, or `strings.ToValidUTF8`) and log it. Add writer tests that parse the output with yaml.v3 for ESC, `\f`, bare CR, CRLF and `\xe9` content and assert byte equality.

## Resolution
YAMLWriter now encodes the header and each entry with gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (indent 2); EscapeForYAML and YAMLFmtFileEntry deleted. Invalid UTF-8 is replaced with U+FFFD once in the processor with a Warn line naming the file. TestStructuredOutputRoundTrips covers ESC, form feed, bare CR, CRLF, DEL, NEL, BOM; TestProcessorReplacesInvalidUTF8 covers Latin-1. PyYAML repros for ESC/CR/CRLF now round-trip byte-for-byte.
title: YAML output is unparseable when any file contains a control character, bare CR or invalid UTF-8, and silently rewrites CRLF to LF

## Problem

Every writer holds the raw `*os.File` and writes directly, so each `WriteString`/`Fprintf` is a separate `write(2)`. The YAML writer formats content one line at a time, which makes one syscall per source line. The JSON and Markdown writers do a few per file. `StartWriter` has no `bufio.Writer` in between.

## Evidence

fileproc/yaml_writer.go:78-80:
```go
lines := strings.Split(body, "\n")
for _, line := range lines {
	if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w.outFile, "      %s\n", line); err != nil {
```
Measured on 300 files × 3,000 lines (22 MB), `-concurrency 4`:
| format | wall time | sys time | write calls (`strace -f -c -e write`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| json | 0.07 s | 0.05 s | 605 |
| markdown | 0.05 s | 0.04 s | not measured |
| yaml | 1.11 s | 0.64 s | 900,301 |

## Impact

YAML output time scales with line count in syscalls, not bytes. A large monorepo dump spends most of its time in the kernel, and the single writer goroutine back-pressures every worker.

## Fix

In `runFormatWriter`, wrap the file once: `bw := bufio.NewWriterSize(outFile, 64<<10)`. Pass `bw` (as an `io.Writer`) to the writer factories, change the writers' field from `*os.File` to `io.Writer`, and call `bw.Flush()` after `Close`, returning its error. The yaml.v3 encoder change in audit-b5d681ab also removes the per-line loop. Add a benchmark for `StartWriter` with the YAML format to keep the regression visible.

## Resolution
runFormatWriter wraps the output in a 64 KiB bufio.Writer and flushes after Close (flush error returned); writers take io.Writer. 22 MB YAML run: 900,301 -> 391 write syscalls, 1.11 s -> 0.61 s. BenchmarkStartWriter covers yaml.
title: Writers write unbuffered to *os.File; YAML issues one write syscall per content line (900k syscalls, 16x slower than JSON on 22 MB)

## Problem

`writeInline` uses `json.Marshal`, and `Start` uses `shared.EscapeForJSON`, which also calls `json.Marshal`. Both apply HTML-safe escaping, so every `<`, `>` and `&` in file content, prefix or suffix becomes a 6-byte `\uXXXX` sequence. The output is still valid JSON, but it is not meant for an HTML page: it is meant for a model. The YAML path already disables this (`enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)` in shared/writers.go:56), so the two formats are inconsistent.

## Evidence

fileproc/json_writer.go:87: `encoded, err := json.Marshal(fileData)`; shared/writers.go:32: `jsonBytes, err := json.Marshal(content)`.

Reproduced: a file with `List<String> a && b > c` produces JSON containing `<` ×1, `&` ×2 and `>` ×2 in place of the literal characters.

## Impact

Generics, HTML/JSX, shell redirects and C++ templates are common in source code, and each occurrence becomes six bytes and several tokens instead of one. The model reads escape sequences instead of code, and the token budget shrinks.

## Fix

Encode with `json.NewEncoder(&buf)` and `SetEscapeHTML(false)` in both `writeInline` and `EscapeForJSON`, and trim the encoder's trailing newline. Add a writer test that asserts `<`, `>` and `&` appear literally and that the document still parses.

## Resolution
JSON writer encodes with json.Encoder SetEscapeHTML(false) via encodeJSON; EscapeForJSON and WriteWithErrorWrap deleted. TestJSONOutputKeepsHTMLCharacters asserts <, >, & are literal and the document is valid.
title: JSON output escapes every <, > and & in source as </>/&, inflating LLM-bound output

## Problem

CLAUDE.md makes revive the mandatory linter, and `make lint` (prek) runs revive and staticcheck. In CI:
- MegaLinter disables `GO_REVIVE` and `GO_GOLANGCI_LINT` and has no staticcheck linter.
- security.yml runs gosec, govulncheck, opengrep, actionlint/zizmor, checkmake, shfmt, yamllint and trivy, but not `make lint-go` or `make lint-static`.

The golangci-lint step that previously covered this ran in security.yml on `main` and was removed on this branch. A change that fails revive or staticcheck now merges green whenever the author's hooks are absent or skipped (`git commit --no-verify`, a web edit, a Renovate PR).

## Evidence

- `rg -n 'revive|staticcheck|lint-go|lint-static|prek|make lint\b' .github/` matches no step that runs either tool.
- .mega-linter.yml:18-23: `DISABLE_LINTERS:` … `- GO_REVIVE` … `- GO_GOLANGCI_LINT`
- `git show main:.github/workflows/security.yml`, lines 96-97: `- name: Run security-focused golangci-lint` / `uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@…`
- CLAUDE.md:34-35: `**Linter**: revive …` / `**Command**: \`make lint\` (prek runs every hook: go vet, revive, staticcheck, …`

## Impact

The 0-issue lint policy is unenforced at merge time. Renovate dependency bumps, which never run local hooks, reach `main` without any Go lint pass.

## Fix

In security.yml, after the mise-action step, add `- name: Go lint` / `run: make lint-go` and `- name: staticcheck` / `run: make lint-static`. mise already installs both from mise.toml. Alternatively, run `make lint` (all prek hooks) as one step, which also gates editorconfig-checker, markdownlint and yamlfmt. CI does not run those either.

## Resolution
security.yml runs make lint-go (go vet + revive) and make lint-static (staticcheck) after mise-action. actionlint + zizmor pass.
title: No CI workflow runs revive or staticcheck: the mandatory Go linters gate only through local hooks

## Problem

`ResetViperConfig` and the CLI integration tests (`run`, `Process`) call `config.LoadConfig()`, which searches `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gibidify` and `$HOME/.config/gibidify`. No test isolates those variables, so the suite's result depends on whatever config the person running it has installed.

## Evidence

testutil/testutil.go:161-167:
```go
func ResetViperConfig(t *testing.T, configPath string) {
	t.Helper()
	config.Reset()
	if configPath != "" {
		config.AddConfigPath(configPath)
	}
	config.LoadConfig()
}
```
Reproduced: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<dir with gibidify/config.yaml: resourceLimits.maxFiles 1, fileSizeLimit 1024, fileTypes.enabled false> go test -count=1 ./...` fails 11 tests:
- `TestRunEnforcesConfiguredMaxConcurrency`, `TestRunMarkdownExecution`, `TestIntegrationFullCLI`, `TestIntegrationCancellation` (root package)
- `TestProcessFailsWhenAFileCannotBeRead`, `TestProcessOutputOrderIsDeterministic`, `TestProcessorvalidateFileCollection`, `TestProcessorProcessIntegration`, `TestProcessorProcessContextCancellation` (cli)
- `TestConfigGettersWithDefaults` (config)
- `TestProcessorLargeFileCancellation` (fileproc)

The same command with an empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` passes every package.

## Impact

Any contributor who uses the tool with a personal config sees spurious failures. The tests also verify behavior under that config rather than the defaults they assert, so a passing run in CI and a failing one locally describe different programs.

## Fix

Isolate the config environment for every package that loads config. Add a `TestMain` to the root, `cli`, `config` and `fileproc` packages that points `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HOME` at an empty `os.MkdirTemp` directory before `m.Run()` and removes it afterwards. Tests that need a config file already pass their own path (`ResetViperConfig(t, dir)`), and it is searched first. Add one config test that installs a restrictive user config, runs `LoadConfig`, and asserts the defaults are not used, so the isolation itself is covered.

## Resolution
testutil.RunIsolated points XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME at an empty temp dir; TestMain in root, cli, config (external pkg), fileproc (external pkg) and testutil calls it. The restrictive user config that failed 11 tests now passes all packages with -race. TestRunIsolatedHidesUserConfig asserts no config file is found.
title: Test suite loads the developer's real ~/.config/gibidify/config.yaml; a valid user config fails 11 tests

## Problem

`shouldSkipFile` returns true for a file larger than `fileSizeLimit` without logging. Collection-time skips are never counted in `runStats`, so the summary line claims nothing was skipped. The size check in `FileProcessor.validateFile`, which does report, is unreachable for these files.

## Evidence

fileproc/file_filters.go:73:
```go
if info, err := entry.Info(); err == nil && info.Size() > f.sizeLimit {
	return true
}
```
Reproduced: tree with `a.go` and a 6,000,000-byte `big.txt` (default limit 5 MiB), run with `-log-level debug`. The output lacks `big.txt`, no log line names it, and the summary prints `Processed 3 files (0 skipped, 0 failed)`.

## Impact

The LLM-bound output is missing a source file, and nothing tells the user. Questions about that file are then answered from absent context, while the tool reports a complete run.

## Fix

Log the skip in `shouldSkipFile` at Warn: `Skipping %s: size %d exceeds fileSizeLimit %d`. A file the user expects is gone, so it must show at the default level. Return the count from collection and fold it into the `skipped` total printed by `Process`. Add a walker test that asserts the log line and the count.

## Resolution
shouldSkipFile logs oversized files at Warn and counts them; ProdWalker.Skipped() and CollectFiles return the count, which Process adds to the skipped total. TestCollectFilesReportsOversizedFiles covers it.
title: Files over fileSizeLimit are dropped at collection with no log line, and the run summary reports 0 skipped

## Problem

Go's `flag` package stops parsing at the first non-flag argument, and `ParseFlags` never checks `fs.NArg()`. Everything after a stray word is dropped without an error, and the run continues on defaults.

## Evidence

cli/flags.go:70-72 parses and returns without inspecting `fs.Args()`:
```go
if err := fs.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
	return nil, err
}
```
Reproduced: `gibidify -source src stray -format yaml -destination out.yaml -no-ui` printed `Format: json`, `Destination: src.json` and the full UI, wrote `src.json`, and exited 0. `out.yaml` was not created.

## Impact

The user gets the wrong format at a different path, and that path, `<basename>.<format>` in the current directory, is overwritten without warning. Typical triggers are a shell glob expanding to extra words, or `gibidify ./src -format yaml` written with the source as an argument.

## Fix

After `fs.Parse`, return a user error when `fs.NArg() > 0`: `unexpected argument %q (flags must come before arguments; use -source <dir>)`. Classify it as a CLI/validation error so main exits 1 with the usage hint. Add a flags test for `-source x stray -format yaml`.

## Resolution
ParseFlags returns a Validation StructuredError (code UNEXPECTED_ARGUMENT) when fs.NArg() > 0; repro exits 1 and writes nothing. Two TestParseFlags cases added; README documents flags-before-arguments.
title: A positional argument silently discards every flag after it

body:
## Problem

The only built-in exclusions are a directory-name list and binary/image extensions. Two consequences:
- Well-known credential files inside the tree (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `*.p12`) are collected unless a `.gitignore` happens to cover them.
- `.git` is excluded only as an entry in the configurable `ignoreDirectories` default. Setting `ignoreDirectories` replaces that list (config.example.yaml:43 documents this), so a user who adds one directory silently re-includes `.git/`, whose `config` holds remote URLs that often carry tokens.

The code's own threat model already treats this exposure as a defect: the symlink rationale in file_filters.go:35-38 names "credentials, keys" reaching "output that is pasted into an LLM".

## Evidence

shared/constants.go:79-82: `ConfigIgnoredDirectoriesDefault = []string{"vendor", "node_modules", ".git", "dist", "build", "target", "bower_components", "cache", "tmp"}`.

Reproduced on a fresh `git init` tree with `.env` (`API_KEY=abc`), `a.go` and a remote `https://user:<token>@example.com/r.git`:
- default config: output files `['.env', 'a.go']`, with no warning
- config `ignoreDirectories: [secrets]`: 20 files, 18 under `.git/`, and the remote token is present in the output

## Impact

Secrets go to a third-party model, and the run reports success. The trigger needs no mistake: a non-git directory, a `.env` the repository never gitignored, or adding a single entry to `ignoreDirectories`.

## Fix

Make VCS metadata unconditional: skip `.git`, `.hg` and `.svn` in `shouldSkipDirectory` regardless of `ignoreDirectories`, and drop `.git` from the configurable default. Add a built-in sensitive-file filter applied in `shouldSkipFile` (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `id_rsa*`, `id_ed25519*`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.pgpass`). Log each skip at Warn, and add a `-include-sensitive` flag as the explicit opt-out. Document both in README. Add walker tests for `.env` and for `.git` with a custom `ignoreDirectories`.

## Resolution
.git/.hg/.svn are skipped unconditionally and .git left the replaceable default list; a built-in credential-file filter (.env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, id_rsa*/id_dsa*/id_ecdsa*/id_ed25519*, .npmrc, .netrc, .pgpass) skips, warns and counts; -include-sensitive opts out. Tests: TestProdWalkerSkipsSensitiveFiles, TestProdWalkerAlwaysSkipsVCSDirectories. Repro: default and custom-ignoreDirectories runs now output only a.go, no token. README "What is included" documents the rules.
title: Credential files reach the LLM-bound output by default: `.env` is always included, and `.git/` (remote-URL tokens) returns once ignoreDirectories is set

## Problem

Two documents contradict the code:
- The `customBinaryExtensions` comment says the built-ins are `.exe, .dll, .so, .dylib, .a, .lib, .obj, .o`. `.obj` is not built in, and the comment omits the other 30 built-ins: `.bin`, `.jar`, `.class`, `.pyc`, `.pyo`, `.dat`, `.db`, `.sqlite`, `.ds_store`, `.pdf`, archives, fonts, audio and video. ## Evidence

- config.example.yaml:81: `# Add custom binary extensions (beyond built-in: .exe, .dll, .so, .dylib, .a, .lib, .obj, .o)`
- fileproc/extensions.go:23-77 (`getBinaryExtensions`) contains `.exe .dll .so .dylib .bin .o .a .lib .jar .class .pyc .pyo .dat .db .sqlite .ds_store .pdf .zip .tar .gz .bz2 .xz .7z .rar .ttf .otf .woff .woff2 .mp3 .mp4 .avi .mov .wmv .flv .webm .ogg .wav .flac`, and no `.obj`.
- CLAUDE.md:13: `**Patterns**: Producer-consumer, thread-safe registry, streaming, modular`, continued at line 14: `(50-200 lines)`.
- Line counts: config/validation.go 373, cli/errors.go 301, config/store.go 269, cli/ui.go 211, shared/constants.go 209, shared/logger.go 205.
- The same line also claims "streaming", but CLAUDE.md:65-66 itself states "there is no streaming path".

Users configure extensions from a wrong list, and `.obj` object files (often large) reach the output. Agents working from CLAUDE.md are given a size rule the code does not follow, and a streaming pattern the same file says does not exist.

## Fix

Replace the parenthetical lists in config.example.yaml:74 and :81 with a pointer to `fileproc/extensions.go`. This removes a second copy of the list that has already drifted. Alternatively, add `.obj` to `getBinaryExtensions` if excluding it was the intent. In CLAUDE.md:13-14, drop "streaming" and the "(50-200 lines)" figure.

config.example.yaml extension comments now point at getImageExtensions/getBinaryExtensions in fileproc/extensions.go instead of a drifted copy; CLAUDE.md Patterns line drops "streaming", "thread-safe" and "(50-200 lines)" and points to docs/audit/arch-profile.md.

- The "With Make" recipe lines are indented with two spaces, and make requires a tab.

## Problem

`PrintSuccess`, `PrintError`, `PrintWarning` and `PrintInfo` call fatih/color's package helpers (`color.Green`, `color.Red`, `color.Yellow`, `color.Blue`). These print to `color.Output`, which is stdout, not `ui.output`. Colors are enabled when stderr is a terminal (`isColorTerminal` → `isInteractiveTerminal` stats `os.Stderr`). So an interactive run writes every status and error line to stdout, contradicting the field comment "Progress and colors go to stderr". `PrintHeader` and the no-color branch use `ui.output` correctly.

## Evidence

cli/ui.go:108-109:
```go
if ui.enableColors {
	color.Green("✓ "+format, args...)
```
Reproduced with stderr on a pty and stdout piped: `gibidify -source src -destination /dev/stdout | cat > piped.out`. `piped.out` (319 bytes) contains `ℹ Format: json` … `ℹ ⚙️  Initializing processing...` followed by the JSON document and then `✓ Processing completed. Output saved to /dev/stdout`, so it is not valid JSON. The same run with `-no-colors` produces valid JSON. Writing to `/dev/stdout` is a supported destination (`removePartialOutput`, cli/processor_processing.go:146-155).

## Impact

`gibidify -source . -destination /dev/stdout | jq …` or `| pbcopy` breaks in a normal terminal. The consumer receives status text mixed into the document. Error messages also land on stdout, where a script capturing stdout swallows them.

## Fix

Write colored output to `ui.output` like `PrintHeader` does. Build each color once (`color.New(color.FgGreen)`) and call `.Fprintf(ui.output, "✓ "+format+"\n", args...)`; delete the package-level `color.Green/Red/Yellow/Blue` calls. Add a UI test that sets `ui.output` to a buffer with colors enabled, asserts the message lands there, and asserts nothing reaches a redirected `os.Stdout`.

## Resolution
All Print* methods go through printStatus, which writes colored text with color.New(attr).Fprintf(ui.output); package-level color helpers removed. TestColoredStatusGoesToOutputNotStdout added. pty repro: -destination /dev/stdout piped is valid JSON while 98 escape sequences reach stderr.
title: With colors on, status messages go to stdout instead of stderr and corrupt `-destination /dev/stdout` output

## Problem

`NewUIManager` sets `enableColors` from `isColorTerminal()` and `enableProgress` from `isInteractiveTerminal()`. `NewProcessor` then overwrites both from the flags alone (`!flags.NoColors && !flags.NoUI`, `!flags.NoProgress && !flags.NoUI`), so detection never takes effect: every run without `-no-colors`/`-no-progress` colors its output and draws the progress bar, whatever stderr is connected to. Colors are suppressed under `NO_COLOR` only because fatih/color's `color.New` checks that variable itself.

## Evidence

cli/processor_types.go:20-21:
```go
ui.SetColorOutput(!flags.NoColors && !flags.NoUI)
ui.SetProgressOutput(!flags.NoProgress && !flags.NoUI)
```
Reproduced with `NO_COLOR` and `CI` unset and `TERM=xterm-256color`: `gibidify -source src -destination o.json 2> stderr.log` writes a 1,031-byte log with 98 ESC sequences and 4 carriage-return progress redraws (`\x1b[1m🚀 Starting gibidify\n\x1b[0m\x1b[34mℹ Format: json…`). Found while verifying the fix for audit-dd8d8c71.

## Impact

CI logs, `2> file` captures and anything else reading stderr receive escape codes and redraw noise. The terminal checks in ui.go are dead logic.

In `NewProcessor`, let the flags only turn features off: `ui.SetColorOutput(ui.enableColors && !flags.NoColors && !flags.NoUI)` and `ui.SetProgressOutput(ui.enableProgress && !flags.NoProgress && !flags.NoUI)`. Add a processor test that runs with stderr redirected to a pipe and asserts both are disabled.

## Resolution
NewProcessor ANDs the flags with NewUIManager's terminal detection, so flags only turn colors/progress off. TestNewProcessor now runs with stderr on a pipe and fixed color env (cases: non-terminal, FORCE_COLOR, no-colors over FORCE_COLOR).
title: NewProcessor forces colors and the progress bar on, overriding terminal detection, so redirected stderr logs get ANSI codes and progress redraws

body:
## Problem

There are two silent no-op paths:
- `validateFileTypeSettings` checks the custom image, binary and language settings but not `disabledImageExtensions`, `disabledBinaryExtensions` or `disabledLanguageExtensions`. A dot-less entry such as `svg` is accepted and matches nothing, because registry keys are `filepath.Ext` results (`.svg`).
- `validateCustomExtensions` validates `strings.TrimSpace(ext)`, but `ApplyCustomExtensions` (fileproc/config.go:26-31) stores the untrimmed value. So `" .foo"` passes validation and is registered as `" .foo"`, which no file extension equals.

## Evidence

config/validation.go:207-211 validates only `ConfigKeyFileTypesCustomImageExtensions`, `ConfigKeyFileTypesCustomBinaryExtensions` and the custom languages; config/validation.go:231 has `ext = strings.TrimSpace(ext)`; fileproc/config.go:29 has `adder(strings.ToLower(ext))`.

Reproduced against a tree with `a.go`, `data.foo` and `logo.svg`:
| config | output files |
| --- | --- |
| none | `a.go`, `data.foo` |
| `disabledImageExtensions: ["svg"]` | `a.go`, `data.foo` (no warning) |
| `disabledImageExtensions: [".svg"]` | `a.go`, `data.foo`, `logo.svg` |
| `customBinaryExtensions: [" .foo"]` | `a.go`, `data.foo` (no warning) |
| `customBinaryExtensions: [".foo"]` | `a.go` |

## Impact

A user who disables or adds an extension and makes a common typo gets the default behavior, with nothing indicating the setting was ignored. That can include a custom binary extension meant to keep files out of the output.

## Fix

Run `validateCustomExtensions` over the three disabled-list keys as well (`validateFileTypeSettings`). Normalise once at the point of use: `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(ext))` in `ApplyCustomExtensions`, `addExtensions` and `DisableExtensions`, and trim the custom language keys the same way. Add validation tests for a dot-less disabled entry, and a registry test showing `" .foo"` registers `.foo`.

## Resolution
validateFileTypeSettings validates the three disabled lists like the custom ones; extensions and language keys are trimmed+lowercased at registration and removal (normalizeConfiguredExtension); ignoreDirectories entries trimmed in NewFileFilter. ## Problem

Several parts of the release config are misleading or inert:
- The build `gibidify-linux-dynamic` is commented "dynamic linking for additional architectures" but sets `CGO_ENABLED=0`, so every binary it produces is statically linked. The only difference from `gibidify-linux-static` is the architecture list.

- The `before` hook runs `go generate ./...`, and the repository has no `//go:generate` directive.
- `goreleaser check` reports that `dockers` and `docker_manifests` "are being phased out and will eventually be replaced by `dockers_v2`".

## Evidence

- .goreleaser.yaml:45-46: `# Linux: dynamic linking for additional architectures` / `- id: gibidify-linux-dynamic`; :73-74: `env:` / `- CGO_ENABLED=0`
- .goreleaser.yaml:27: `- -extldflags=-static`, with `CGO_ENABLED=0` at :36
- .goreleaser.yaml:13: `- go generate ./...`; `rg -n '//go:generate' --type go` returns no match
- `mise exec -- goreleaser check` prints the dockers deprecation notice twice and exits 0

## Impact

A reader picks the "dynamic" build expecting a glibc-linked binary, or keeps two build blocks believing the linking differs. The deprecated `dockers` blocks will stop working in a future GoReleaser major version, which then fails a tagged release.

Merge the two Linux builds into one `gibidify-linux` build listing all architectures (amd64 included) with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, and drop the `-extldflags=-static` ldflag. One gibidify-linux build (CGO_ENABLED=0, all arches); -extldflags=-static and the go generate hook removed; dockers + docker_manifests migrated to one dockers_v2 entry (amd64, arm64, arm/v7) with Dockerfile.release, which has no RUN step so it builds without QEMU (the old arm RUN apk failed with exec format error). goreleaser check: no deprecations; goreleaser release --snapshot --clean succeeded; image runs as 10001:10001.

## Problem

`matchesIgnoreRules` returns true as soon as any rule set on the ancestor path matches. In git, the deepest matching pattern decides, so `!keep.log` in `sub/.gitignore` overrides `*.log` from the root. Here the root rule wins and the negation is never consulted.

## Evidence

fileproc/ignore_rules.go:52-56:
```go
for _, rule := range rules {
	if matchesRule(fullPath, isDir, rule) {
		return true
	}
}
```
Reproduced: root `.gitignore` `*.log`, `sub/.gitignore` `!keep.log`. `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists `sub/keep.log`; gibidify's output omits it.

## Impact

Files a repository deliberately keeps (whitelisted logs, fixtures, generated-but-committed files) are left out of the output, with no message.

## Fix

Evaluate rules deepest-first and let the first file with an opinion decide. go-gitignore cannot report a lone negation: `MatchesPathHow` (ignore.go:217-237 at the pinned version) returns `(false, nil)` for both "re-included" and "no match". So when loading each ignore file in `tryLoadIgnoreFile`, also compile its `!` lines with the `!` stripped into a second matcher (`neg`). In `matchesIgnoreRules`, iterate `rules` in reverse: if `rule.gi` matches, the path is ignored; else if `rule.neg` matches, it is included; otherwise ask the parent rule. Add a walker test for the parent `*.log` / child `!keep.log` case.

## Resolution
Each ignore file also compiles its "!" patterns (stripped) into a neg matcher; matchesIgnoreRules checks rules deepest-first (slices.Backward) and the first with an opinion decides. TestProdWalkerNestedNegationReincludes covers parent *.log / child !keep.log.
title: A nested .gitignore cannot re-include a file its parent ignores (`!pattern` is ignored across files)

## Problem

These tests cannot fail on a regression:
- `TestIsInteractiveTerminal` discards its result.
- `TestMainPackageExports` only calls `t.Log`.
- `TestFileTypeRegistryConcurrentModifications` gives every goroutine its own new registry, so nothing is shared and no concurrency is exercised.

It also calls `CreateTestFile`/`CreateTestDirectory`, which call `t.Fatalf`, from spawned goroutines. `FailNow` must run on the test goroutine: from another one it exits only that goroutine, the `done <- true` send is skipped, and the test blocks until the `go test` timeout.

## Evidence

- cli/ui_test.go:460-468: `result := isInteractiveTerminal()` … `_ = result`
- main_coverage_test.go:50-61: three `t.Log` lines, no check
- fileproc/filetypes_concurrency_test.go:122-123: `// Create a new registry instance for this goroutine` / `registry := createConcurrencyTestRegistry()`
- testutil/concurrency_test.go:18-21:
```go
go func(n int) {
	CreateTestFile(t, tempDir, fmt.Sprintf("%c", 'a'+n)+".txt", []byte("content"))
	done <- true
}(i)
```
- testutil/testutil.go:100-101: `CreateTestFile` calls `t.Fatalf` on a write error.

## Impact

Coverage is credited for code that no assertion checks. A broken `CreateTestFile` turns into a 10-minute hang instead of a failure, and the race detector is never given a shared registry to check.

Delete `TestMainPackageExports`. Replace `TestIsInteractiveTerminal` with a test that sets `os.Stderr` to a pipe (`os.Pipe`) and asserts false. Point `TestFileTypeRegistryConcurrentModifications` at one shared registry doing concurrent reads (`IsBinary`, `Language`) after configuration, which is the access pattern registry.go documents. Run under `-race`, and delete the per-goroutine-registry variant. In `TestConcurrentOperations`, collect errors with `os.WriteFile`/`os.Mkdir` inside the goroutines (or use `errgroup`), report them with `t.Errorf` after `wg.Wait()`, and assert that the 10 paths exist.

## Resolution
Deleted TestMainPackageExports and the per-goroutine-registry TestFileTypeRegistryConcurrentModifications (TestFileTypeRegistryConcurrentReads already covers shared-registry reads under -race); TestIsInteractiveTerminal replaced by TestIsInteractiveTerminalFalseForPipe; TestConcurrentOperations collects errors from goroutines and asserts all 10 paths exist.

## Problem

`createOutputFile` calls `os.Create` on the destination before any file is processed, which truncates an existing output. On cancellation or a write error, `removePartialOutput` then deletes it. A re-run that does not complete therefore leaves no output at all, not the last good one. The cancellation error is not a `StructuredError` and matches none of `IsUserError`'s patterns, so `main` prints "An unexpected error occurred. Please check the logs." and exits 2. A user-initiated Ctrl-C conventionally exits 130 with no error banner.

## Evidence

cli/processor_processing.go:161: `outFile, err := os.Create(filepath.Clean(p.flags.Destination))`; :117-118: `if writeErr != nil || sendErr != nil { p.removePartialOutput() }`; main.go:48-52 is the exit-2 branch.

Reproduced on a 22 MB tree: a first run writes `keep.yaml` (27,253,719 bytes, exit 0). Re-running the same command and sending SIGINT after 0.3 s gives exit 2, and `keep.yaml` no longer exists.

## Impact

An aborted regeneration destroys a usable artifact that scripts, hooks (the pre-commit example in examples/basic-usage.md) or a user depend on. Interrupting is reported as an internal failure.

## Fix

Write to a temporary file in the destination's directory (`os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(dest), "."+filepath.Base(dest)+".*")`) and `os.Rename` it over the destination only after the writer and `Close` succeed. On failure, remove only the temp file. Keep writing directly when the destination is not a regular file (`/dev/stdout`). In `main`, check `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` before the user/system split: print "Interrupted" and exit 130. Add a processor test that pre-creates the destination, cancels mid-run, and asserts the original bytes survive.

## Resolution
createOutputFile writes to os.CreateTemp in the destination's directory (0600, or the replaced file's mode) and commit() renames it over the destination only on success; discard() removes it otherwise; non-regular destinations are written directly. main maps context.Canceled to "Interrupted" and exit 130. Tests: TestProcessCanceledKeepsPreviousOutput, TestProcessReplacesOutputAndKeepsMode, TestIntegrationCancellation. Repro: SIGINT re-run exits 130 and the 25 MB output keeps its SHA-256.
title: An interrupted or failed re-run deletes the previous good output, and Ctrl-C is reported as "An unexpected error occurred" (exit 2)

## Problem

The binary statically links ten third-party modules:
- MIT: fatih/color, mattn/go-colorable, mattn/go-isatty, mitchellh/colorstring, rivo/uniseg, sabhiram/go-gitignore, schollz/progressbar.
- BSD-3-Clause: golang.org/x/sys, golang.org/x/term.
- MIT + Apache-2.0: gopkg.in/yaml.v3, which ships a NOTICE file.

## Evidence

- .goreleaser.yaml:200-202: archive `files:` lists `- LICENSE` and `- README.md`; nfpms `contents` (lines 305-309) installs only those two.
- The Dockerfile and the goreleaser inline Dockerfiles copy only the binary.
- yaml.v3's LICENSE line 2: "This project is covered by two different licenses: MIT and Apache."; its NOTICE: "Copyright 2011-2016 Canonical Ltd. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0".
- `go list -deps` over the main package resolves the ten modules listed.

## Impact

Every published release redistributes third-party code without the attribution its licenses require.

## Fix

Generate the notices from the linked dependency set rather than by hand: add a goreleaser `before` hook `go run github.com/google/go-licenses/v2@<pinned> report . --template <tmpl> > THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` (or commit the file and regenerate it when go.mod changes). scripts/third-party-notices.sh builds THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES from go list -deps (license + NOTICE of all 10 linked modules, incl. yaml.v3's Canonical NOTICE); goreleaser before-hook runs it; included in archives, nfpms (/usr/share/doc/gibidify) and both Dockerfiles. Snapshot release verified in tar.gz, .deb and image.

body:
## Problem

`collectFiles` excludes the destination by `filepath.Abs`, and the walker builds paths from `filepath.Abs(source)` plus entry names. Neither side resolves symlinks. When the source is named through a symlink and the destination through the real path (or the reverse), the strings differ, the exclusion never matches, and the previous run's output is collected as input.

## Evidence

cli/processor_collection.go:17:
```go
if absDest, err := shared.AbsolutePath(p.flags.Destination); p.flags.Destination != "" && err == nil {
```
`shared.AbsolutePath` is `filepath.Abs` (shared/paths.go:12-19). Reproduced: `link -> real`, run twice `gibidify -source link -destination real/out.json -no-ui`. The second run's output lists files `['a.go', 'out.json']`.

## Impact

Each run embeds the previous output, so the output grows on every run and the LLM receives a duplicated copy of the tree. This only triggers when the source and destination name the tree through different paths.

## Fix

Exclude by file identity, not by name. Before collecting, `os.Stat` the destination (when it exists) and keep its `os.FileInfo`. In `shouldSkipEntry`, compare candidates with `os.SameFile(entryInfo, destInfo)`. This covers symlinked roots, bind mounts and hard links. When the destination does not exist yet, nothing can be ingested from it on this run, so the lexical check can stay as is. Add a walker test that builds the symlinked-root layout.

## Resolution
FileFilter stats existing excluded paths and skips files that os.SameFile matches, besides the lexical check. TestProdWalkerExcludesByIdentity covers the symlinked root; repro's second run outputs only a.go.
title: Output exclusion compares lexical paths, so a destination reached through a symlinked source is ingested on the next run

body:
## Problem

`validateFile` checks the path with `os.Lstat` (regular file, size), and `readCapped` then opens the same path by name with `os.Open`, which follows symlinks. A file replaced between the two calls by a symlink to a path outside the tree is read through the link. A file replaced by a FIFO makes the open block, and the run hangs. The comment at lines 67-69 states that such a swap "is refused rather than followed".

## Evidence

fileproc/processor.go:75: `fileInfo, err := os.Lstat(filePath)`, then fileproc/processor.go:148: `f, err := os.Open(filepath.Clean(filePath))`. The check and the use are separate path lookups.

## Impact

This needs something writing to the scanned tree during the run, such as a build, a sync client, or a hostile checkout script. When that happens, the walker's symlink containment, which keeps credentials outside the tree out of LLM-bound output, can be bypassed, or the run can hang.

## Fix

Check the descriptor, not the name. Open with `os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_NONBLOCK, 0)`, behind a build-tagged helper that falls back to plain `os.Open` on Windows. Then `f.Stat()` the open file and apply the regular-file and size checks to that `FileInfo`, deleting the separate `Lstat` pre-check. Add a unix test that replaces a file with a symlink and asserts the read is refused.

## Resolution
ProcessWithContext opens once via openNoFollow (unix: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, ELOOP/EMLINK -> ErrSkipped; other: Lstat then Open) and validates the open descriptor with f.Stat(); the separate Lstat check is gone. TestProcessorRefusesSymlink passes; builds for linux, darwin, freebsd and windows vet.
title: Lstat-then-Open leaves a window where a path swapped for a symlink or FIFO is followed or blocks

body:
## Problem

`isColorTerminal` reads five environment variables to decide whether status output is colored:
- `TERM` empty or `dumb` disables color.
- Any `CI` disables it unless `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.
- `NO_COLOR` disables it.
- `FORCE_COLOR` enables it.

The README documents only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and the `--no-colors`/`--no-ui` flags, so a user cannot tell why colors appear in one environment and not another, or that `FORCE_COLOR` exists. Colored output also changes which stream status lines reach (audit-dd8d8c71).

## Evidence

- cli/ui.go:168, :174, :176, :184 and :189 read `TERM`, `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `NO_COLOR` and `FORCE_COLOR`.
- `rg -l NO_COLOR README.md examples/ config.example.yaml` and the same for `FORCE_COLOR`, `TERM` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` match nothing.
- Behavior was checked on a pty: no env → 11 escape-coded lines; `NO_COLOR=1` → 0, also with `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.

## Impact

Color behavior differs between a terminal, CI and GitHub Actions with no documented reason or override.

## Fix

Add an "Environment" list to README.md under Usage covering:
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`HOME` (config search).
- `NO_COLOR` (disables color, per no-color.org).
- `FORCE_COLOR` (enables color off a TTY).
- `TERM=dumb` (disables color).
- `CI` (disables color except on GitHub Actions).

## Resolution
README "Environment" section documents XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME, NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, TERM=dumb and CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS.
title: Environment variables that change output (NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, TERM, CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS) are undocumented

## Problem

Several layers exist without a second implementation or caller to justify them:
- `shared.Logger` declares 11 methods, and its only implementation, `logService`, wraps `*slog.Logger`. Production code never calls `Debug`, `Warn` or `Error` (the non-`f` forms), and `WithFields` has one caller (`LogError`). Reference counts over comment-stripped sources:
| symbol | production | test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.Debug(` | 0 | 4 |
| `.Warn(` | 0 | 4 |
| `.Error(` | 0 | 7 |
| `.WithFields(` | 1 | 2 |
| `.Extension` (read) | 0 | 0 |

## Problem

`tryLoadIgnoreFile` discards the error from `ignore.CompileIgnoreFile` and returns nil, so the walk continues as if the directory had no ignore file. The justifying comment, "Regex compile error handled by validation, safe to ignore here", is wrong on both counts:
- Nothing validates ignore files.
- `CompileIgnoreFile`'s only error is the read error. go-gitignore drops bad patterns itself (`pattern, _ := regexp.Compile(expr)`, ignore.go:144).

git warns `unable to access '.gitignore'` in this case.

## Evidence

fileproc/ignore_rules.go:38-39:
```go
// Regex compile error handled by validation, safe to ignore here
if gi, err := ignore.CompileIgnoreFile(ignorePath); err == nil {
```
Reproduced: tree `a.go`, `secret.env` and `.gitignore` containing `secret.env`.
- Readable: output `['.gitignore', 'a.go']`.
- After `chmod 000 .gitignore`: output `['a.go', 'secret.env']`.

The only error printed is that `.gitignore` itself "could not be processed" as a content file. Nothing says its rules were not applied.

## Impact

Files a repository deliberately excludes, such as credentials and generated secrets, reach the LLM-bound output when an ignore file has restrictive permissions. A sync tool, a container UID mismatch or a root-owned checkout can set those permissions.

## Fix

Return the error from `tryLoadIgnoreFile` when the file exists but cannot be compiled (read). Have `walkDir` fail the walk at the root, and for subdirectories skip the whole directory with a Warn line, the same way an unreadable directory is handled at walker.go:86-90: an unapplied ignore file must not widen what is collected. Replace the comment with the real reason. Add a walker test with a mode-000 `.gitignore` asserting the excluded file is absent and a warning is logged.

## Resolution
tryLoadIgnoreFile returns read errors; walkDir fails at the root and below it the directory is skipped with a Warn line (existing unreadable-directory path). Wrong comment replaced. TestProdWalkerUnreadableIgnoreFile covers both cases.
title: An unreadable .gitignore/.ignore is silently skipped, so the files it excludes are written to the output

## Problem

The README's only description of what is left out is "Symlinks are never followed, and files whose first bytes contain a NUL byte are skipped as binary." It does not say that `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files at every level are honoured, that files over `fileSizeLimit` (5 MB) are dropped, which directories are skipped by default, or that binary/image extensions are skipped. ## Evidence

- shared/constants.go:79-82 holds the default directory list.
- `rg -n -i 'gitignore|\.ignore' README.md` returns no match.

## Impact

A user cannot predict the contents of the output without reading the code. A missing file looks like a bug, and an unwanted file (a non-gitignored secret) looks like it should have been excluded.

## Fix

Add a "What is included" subsection after README.md:69. It should list the exclusion rules in order: symlinks and non-regular files; `ignoreDirectories` (with the default list); `.gitignore`/`.ignore` at every level; binary/image extensions; files over `fileSizeLimit`; NUL-byte content. It should also say that the destination file is excluded.

## Resolution
README "What is included" lists every exclusion rule in order, plus the destination exclusion and UTF-8 handling.
